content: The QTc interval can be prolonged by quinine, necessitating caution and close monitoring. Avoid using quinine with other drugs that also prolong the QT interval or in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. Post-marketing reports indicate that QT prolongation has occurred in cases of overdose, particularly in patients with concurrent illnesses or those taking drugs that cause electrolyte imbalances or prolong the QT interval. Quinidine increases quinine levels by competing for renal tubular clearance, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Similarly, quizartinib and quinine enhance each other's effects on the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification and frequent ECG monitoring. Ranolazine and quinine also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ribociclib increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended, especially when co-administered with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Rifabutin and rifampin decrease quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Quinine increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Rilpivirine increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use rilpivirine cautiously with drugs that carry a risk of Torsades de Pointes. Risperidone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Ritlecitinib increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating therapy modification and monitoring. Ritlecitinib also inhibits CYP3A4 substrates, increasing their plasma concentrations and risk of adverse reactions. Romidepsin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Rucaparib increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating therapy adjustments and monitoring. Sarecycline increases quinine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring monitoring for toxicities and potential dose reductions of P-glycoprotein substrates. Sarilumab may alter CYP450 enzyme activity by modulating cytokine levels, such as IL-6, which can affect drug metabolism. Caution is advised when initiating or discontinuing sarilumab in patients taking CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. Schisandra increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Secukinumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme activity by reducing inflammation-related cytokine levels. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing secukinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates. Quinine increases selexipag levels by reducing its metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments and close monitoring. Selpercatinib increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Sertraline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Preand post-colonoscopy ECGs should be considered in high-risk patients. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate has similar effects and monitoring requirements. Solifenacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Somapacitan decreases quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Growth hormone treatments, such as somatrogon and somatropin, may increase CYP450-mediated drug clearance, requiring caution with sensitive CYP substrates. Sorafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Sotalol and quinine also prolong the QTc interval, requiring similar precautions. St. John’s Wort decreases quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Stiripentol increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, requiring therapy adjustments and monitoring for adverse reactions. Sunitinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Tacrolimus and quinine also prolong the QTc interval, requiring similar precautions. Quinine increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Talquetamab increases quinine levels by suppressing CYP enzyme activity during cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Quinine increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Tazemetostat decreases quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while quinine increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required. Teclistamab increases quinine levels by suppressing CYP450 enzyme activity during cytokine release. Monitor for increased concentrations or toxicities of sensitive CYP substrates. Tecovirimat decreases quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring for effectiveness. Telavancin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Telotristat ethyl decreases quinine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments and monitoring for suboptimal efficacy. Tetracaine and quinine may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia, requiring monitoring for symptoms. Thiothixene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Quinine increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Tobramycin and quinine increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, necessitating therapy modification and avoidance of concurrent use. Toremifene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Triclabendazole and quinine also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating similar precautions. Trimipramine and quinine have similar effects, requiring caution and monitoring. Trofinetide increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating monitoring for toxicities. Tucatinib increases quinine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring dose adjustments and monitoring for serious toxicities. Turmeric increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ustekinumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme activity by reducing inflammation-related cytokine levels. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates. Vardenafil and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Viloxazine increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating dose adjustments and monitoring. Voclosporin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Vonoprazan increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Voriconazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Vorinostat and quinine have similar effects, necessitating similar precautions. Quinine increases warfarin levels by inhibiting metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring for enhanced anticoagulant effects. Ziprasidone and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring.
